label: first copy-phase step (after <DEL>) when the fed-back first token is q, L>=5
explanation: Fires only at step t = L+1, the first copy step after <DEL>, where the model has just output the first original token and the input is that token fed back. It fires essentially only when that token is q (first_tok q, 32x lift), and only for L >= 5. For L = 3-4 it is silent, and at L = 5 it fires on just some sequences, so most of the false positives are short sequences. Magnitude grows with L: L=5 holds 2.4% of the mass, and L=8-9 hold about 30% each, with top activations in L=9 sequences. It does not depend on the token being output at this step or the next. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, at any other copy position, or on a q seen elsewhere in the sequence. The 77 missed activations are near zero (rarely more than 0.04 of max) and come from other first tokens such as 2, y and g.

issues: All 723 test false positives are at L=5, step 6. L==5 alone has precision 0.72. L>=6 has precision 1.0 but recall only 0.85, so the L=5 cases cannot be dropped. Conditioning on correct, in_count, n_digits, next_out (digit/vowel) or orig(1)/orig(4) gives no clean split (precision 0.64-0.83). The partial firing at L=5 looks like the weakest activations falling below threshold, not a separate token or history pattern. The explanation already says this.
Minor overclaim: 'never fires at any other copy position' is not strictly true. 13 dev activations are at recall_idx 2 (t=11, L=9), but they carry about 0% of the activation mass.
The 90 test misses are all near zero (0.00-0.05 relative to max). They sit at step 10 of L=9 sequences on first tokens 2, a, u and 3. This is scattered noise and holds 0.0% of the mass.

Magnitude-by-L claims hold: L=5 holds 0.024 of the mass, L=8 0.282 and L=9 0.316. L=3-4 never fire. The feature is silent in the original and delimiter phases. in_tok q has 32x lift. Test scores are P 0.947 / R 0.993 / F1 0.970 / mass recall 0.9996.
